texts: mixed: the lighting, both participants and all three time terms (day 380, Year 2, sundown) are recorded, but two things go wrong. 'lit' lemmatizes to the symbol light, which is also the symbol the mist-light's genus uses later in the passage, so the lighting event and the illumination kind collapse onto one word; and the Harbor Station gets its name but no kind atom saying it is a station. Rewrite as 'On day 380 of Year 2, Coraline Ash kindled the lantern of the Harbor Station at sundown.' to clear the collision - the untyped station is a translator slip (the very same name shape is typed correctly in the sibling passages), not something your wording causes.
good. the burning is recorded with the lantern as the actor and mire-essence as what it consumes, plus the mire_essence to essence genus.
good. the producing event, the lantern as its agent and the mist-light it brings into being are all there, with mist_light linked to light as its genus.
good. the showing, the mist-light as what is shown, and 'at night' as a time slot are all recorded, and the mist-light is the same one the previous sentence introduced.
good. the attracting is recorded with the mist-light as the attractor and a group of nightmoths as what is drawn, plus the nightmoth to moth genus.

mixed: the gathering, the crowd of nightmoths and the Harbor Row location are all recorded, but the Harbor Row gets only its name - no atom says it is a row, so the place stays untyped. This is a translator slip rather than a wording problem (the same name shape is typed correctly in the sibling passages), so no rewrite is really needed; if you want the kind guaranteed, putting the kind word outside the name - 'A crowd of nightmoths gathered at the row called Harbor Row.' - forces it.
good. the pair is recorded as a two-member group with a count of 2 and a per-cat rule, so each sky-cat's own descent is derivable, and the cliff-spires are correctly the source.

bad: 'at the Harbor Row' is dropped altogether - neither the hunting nor the crowd is placed there, so a location you stated reaches the knowledge base nowhere. Front the locative so it can only attach to the hunting: 'At the Harbor Row, the two sky-cats hunted the nightmoth crowd.'

bad: the restrictor 'at the Harbor Row' is dropped here too; it is the same fact the previous sentence states, so one recorded location would cover both, but as things stand neither sentence records it. Front it here as well: 'At the Harbor Row, the nightmoth crowd shrank.' - fronted, it lands on the shrinking event instead of being lost inside the noun phrase.

bad: 'left' is read as the threads being altered by the leaving - both in the flat atoms and in the copied per-moth rule - when the sentence says only that they were deposited and stayed there. Rewrite with a plain deposition verb: 'The nightmoths deposited silken threads on the lantern.'
good. the collecting, the threads, the lantern as the source, and all three time terms (dawn, day 381, Year 2) are covered, with the threads correctly recorded as unchanged by the collecting.
good. Hesper's name, the boiling, the sea-water, and the day 381 of Year 2 date are all recorded, and the threads are correctly the thing the boiling changes.

good. the forming, the cauldron, the 'by evening' deadline as an at-most bound, and the past tense are all covered. One caveat you cannot write around: the mire-essence here is a fresh portion with no link back to the mire-essence the lantern burned in sentence 2 - a bare mass subject has no stated routing, so one mention becomes a witness and the other the bare kind symbol.

good. the drawing, the participial 'stored' kept as a property of the essence, and all three time terms (sundown, day 381, Year 2) are covered, and the essence is the same one the previous sentence formed.
